title: A closed subspace is a limit of finitely presented closed subspaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. A morphism is quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space and let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, algebraic spaces $X_a$ over $Y$, closed immersions $i_a:X_a\hookrightarrow Y$ of finite presentation, and compatible closed immersion transitions $r_{ba}:X_b\hookrightarrow X_a$ for $a\le b$. There are compatible closed immersions $q_a:X\hookrightarrow X_a$ satisfying $i_aq_a=i$ and $r_{ba}q_b=q_a$, and the cone $(q_a)$ exhibits $X=\varprojlim_aX_a$ in algebraic spaces over $Y$.

proof.text: The quasi-compact atlas $U\to Y$ makes $|Y|$ quasi-compact in the topological sense required by the module-approximation lemma: pull an open cover of $|Y|$ back to $|U|$, take a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity on points. The inverse images are open by the atlas topology. The absolute diagonal of $Y$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, so the other hypothesis of that lemma is also satisfied.

source.place: Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), implication from a quasi-compact surjective etale atlas

proof.text: By the ideal/closed-subspace correspondence let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_X)$, a quasi-coherent ideal, so $X=V(\mathcal I)$. Apply finite-presentation module approximation to $\mathcal I$: obtain a small filtered diagram of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F_j$ and maps $u_j:\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal I$ which exhibit $\mathcal I$ as a colimit in all $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0A0U (lemma-closed-is-limit-closed-and-finite-presentation), first sentence; Tag 0829 (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type), proof using Tag 07V9 (lemma-colimit-finitely-presented)

proof.text: Let $I$ be the poset of finite-type quasi-coherent submodules $\mathcal I_a\subseteq\mathcal I$, ordered by inclusion. Each is an ideal of $\mathcal O_Y$, since its inclusion into $\mathcal O_Y$ is linear. This is a small set in the chosen larger universe: on the chosen small site submodules are families of subsets of the sets $\mathcal I(U)$ subject to the module and restriction conditions. It contains $0$. For $a,b$, the image of $\mathcal I_a\oplus\mathcal I_b\to\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent upper bound; on affine etale charts it is generated by the union of the two finite generating lists, hence is of finite type. Thus $I$ is nonempty and directed. Also $\mathcal G_j=\operatorname{im}(u_j)$ belongs to $I$: it is quasi-coherent, and on each affine etale chart its generators are the images of a finite generating list for $\mathcal F_j$. In particular every $u_j$ factors through some $\mathcal I_a$ via its image.

source.place: Tag 0829 (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type), proof: finite sums and images of finite-presentation modules

proof.text: For $a\in I$ put $X_a=V(\mathcal I_a)\subseteq Y$ by the ideal/closed-subspace correspondence. Its ideal is exactly $\mathcal I_a$, so the finite-type-ideal criterion says that $i_a:X_a\hookrightarrow Y$ is of finite presentation. This is finite presentation of the morphism to $Y$, without any Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 0A0U (lemma-closed-is-limit-closed-and-finite-presentation), construction of the stages; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 084Q (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation)

proof.text: If $a\le b$, a map to $X_b$ kills $\mathcal I_b$ and therefore $\mathcal I_a$, so the subfunctor descriptions give a unique inclusion $r_{ba}:X_b\to X_a$ over $Y$. They also identify $X_b\times_YX_a$ with $X_b$: a map to the first factor already gives the unique map to the second. Hence $r_{ba}$ is the pullback of the closed immersion $i_b$ and is closed: each scheme test is a scheme test of $i_b$. The same argument with $\mathcal I_a\subseteq\mathcal I$ gives a closed immersion $q_a:X\to X_a$. Uniqueness of maps into these subfunctors gives all transition identities and $i_aq_a=i$, $r_{ba}q_b=q_a$.

source.place: Tag 0A0U (lemma-closed-is-limit-closed-and-finite-presentation), omitted transition and cone checks; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals)

proof.text: To prove the limit universal property, take any algebraic space $T$ over $Y$ with structure map $h:T\to Y$. A compatible cone $T\to X_a$ gives, by the factorization criterion, zero maps $\mathcal I_a\to h_*\mathcal O_T$ for every $a$. Write $d:\mathcal I\to h_*\mathcal O_T$ for the canonical map. Each $u_j$ factors through its finite-type image $\mathcal G_j=\mathcal I_a$, so $d u_j=0$. Since the $u_j$ are a colimit cocone in all module sheaves, maps out of $\mathcal I$ are determined by these composites; comparing $d$ with the zero map gives $d=0$. The same factorization criterion now gives a unique map $T\to V(\mathcal I)=X$ over $Y$. Its composites with $q_a$ equal the given maps, since $X_a$ is a subfunctor of $Y$. Conversely every map $T\to X$ supplies such a cone. This proves the required universal property in algebraic spaces over $Y$; it does not assume an independently existing inverse limit or that pullback is left exact.
